Subtract the Basement scene relocation base from every split scene pointer, then retire this one-shot routine
Inputs: $4D71 = pointer count; $4D72/$4D73 = 16-bit relocation base; split pointers at $4DB4/$4DB5 for indices below $80 and $4EBA/$4EBB for indices $80 and above

Where the relocation loop really starts. As the level is loaded, $816D-$816E hold LDA #$00, so the count at $1E starts from zero here; once every pointer is done, $8178-$817A write RTS ($60) over that LDA, so in a snapshot taken during play $816D reads RTS and $816E keeps the old $00.

Select the current area's recursive scene tree and render its clipped 30-by-18-cell view with palette/reflection transformations
Inputs: area index $A2; area root table $4D74; background table $4D75; relocated split scene pointers $4DB4/$4DB5 and $4EBA/$4EBB; the scene base $4D71, added to the pointer as the immediates #$E4/#$4D at $81DB and $81E0
Outputs: root pointer $02/$03 and renderer bounds/depth/offset state are initialized; recursive records are traversed and their leaves update bitmap, screen, and color work memory
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, recursive stack use, scene pointers and renderer scratch including $02/$03, $0A, $1A/$1B, $38, $DC, and $E7

Render room A in the Basement playable phase, entering the normal scene renderer after its usual load from $A2.
Inputs: A is a valid room index; relocated scene pointers, renderer workspace, bitmap/screen/color buffers, and the active phase are initialized.
Outputs: Selects the room's scene pointer, writes its background color to $D021, traverses the scene-record tree, and renders the room.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, renderer scratch, and VIC-II-visible bitmap/screen/color work memory.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background-color register $D021 and display memory; no CIA access.

Interpret and render a scene-record tree. Inputs: $02/$03 record pointer and initialized renderer workspace. Outputs: bitmap, screen, color, and traversal state are updated. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer zero-page scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible bitmap, screen, and color RAM; no direct VIC-II register write is required.

Dispatch the current encoded scene record for the Basement playable phase, restoring a parent record at nested terminators and returning at the outer terminator.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at the current record; $1A/$1B hold the composite origin; $38 is nesting depth; nested parent frames are on the stack.
Outputs: Decodes nonterminal records; $FF at depth zero returns, while nested $FF restores the parent frame, advances $02/$03, and continues dispatch.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and restored stack bytes.
Hardware: No direct register write here; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Advance over the current Basement playable-phase scene record and resume the scene-record dispatch loop.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a valid encoded record with length/control bits in bytes +1 and +2.
Outputs: Adds the record's encoded length to $02/$03 and tail-jumps back to scene dispatch.
Clobbers: A, Y, N, V, Z, C, and $02/$03; X is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; when subsequent records render, the resumed renderer updates VIC-II-visible display memory.
Advance $02/$03 to the next encoded scene record. Inputs: $02/$03 points at a valid record header. Outputs: $02/$03 points at the following record. Clobbers: A, Y, flags, and $02/$03.

Decode and render the nonterminal Basement playable-phase scene record at $02/$03, including nested composite records.
Inputs: $02/$03 point at a non-$FF record; $1A/$1B hold its origin; relocated scene-pointer tables and renderer buffers are initialized.
Outputs: Decodes position/reflection fields, resolves child or leaf pointers, renders the record, and advances or resumes the enclosing scene tree.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$05, $1A/$1B, $25/$26, $38, renderer scratch, and nesting stack state.
Hardware: No CIA access; descendant rendering changes VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen-code, and color memory.

Draw the picture (scene leaf) that $04/$05 point at, for the Basement playable phase: every leaf of a scene tree falls into it from $829B-$82A5, and DrawUiImageRecord jumps to it at $ABF8 to draw a status-panel picture.
Inputs: $04/$05 point at the picture (first byte width and height nibbles, then its bitmap, screen and colour bytes); $25/$26 hold its column and row and $E8 bit 7 mirrors it; $E7/$DC are the clipping width and height; $02/$03 point at the record that placed it, whose byte 2 bits 5-6 give the number of colour-swap bytes that follow byte 2.
Outputs: Draws the visible cells into the bitmap, screen RAM, colour RAM and the colour copy at $0800, with the colour swaps applied; a picture wholly outside the window is skipped. Then it jumps to AdvanceSceneRecordAndContinue ($820F), which steps $02/$03 past the placing record and resumes the scene-record dispatch loop.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02-$09, coordinate/renderer scratch, and display work memory.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register write; it stores the bitmap, screen-code and colour bytes itself, and calls the resident compositor at $1411 for cells whose colours must be merged.

EngineEntry: The Basement's play code starts here, from PhaseHandoff at $3FF3. It sets $AA to $FF, which lets the interrupt routine play the tune, relocates the scene pointers, clears the scene buffers, waits 25 ticks, lowers the sprite curtain over the play window (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), draws the credits card, sets the background to black, raises the curtain again and waits until it is gone (RaiseSpriteCurtain, $87E0), which shows the card, then waits for the fire button or the second button read through the SID's pot X ($D419), keeping which in $AC, and goes on into EnterArea ($8654) and the main loop. Central Park's EngineEntry also sets $03CB to 1; this one leaves it alone.

Reinitialize the Basement playable phase's scene buffers after GAME OVER and rejoin engine startup immediately before the common gameplay-entry tail. Its one caller is $87A5, reached when the last life is lost and no spare life is left.
Inputs: The death sequence has finished; resident state and the active phase occupant remain valid.
Outputs: Calls the phase scene-buffer initializer, clears $D021 to black, redraws the credit/title card (RenderCreditTitleCard, $8565, which clears the play window first), and continues at the engine's input/frame-loop setup at $8639.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, scene/gameplay initialization state, and helper scratch.
Hardware: Writes VIC-II background color $D021 and updates display/input state through the joined engine-start tail.

Set up the current area and enter the main loop, for The Basement. This runs once each time an area is entered or redrawn, not once a frame: it is reached by falling through from the start-up wait at $8652, from MainTick when the redraw latch $02A9 is set ($8701) and after a lost life ($8768), and it falls into MainTick ($86AE), the per-tick loop.
Inputs: Current area $A2, the player's position and the actor/object state.
Outputs: Sets $0230=$7F; rebuilds the area's enemy meter when $012D,X holds $80-$FE and loads $022A from the area's enemy energy at $3F92; clears the play window and draws the area's scene ($8CF7); clears the actor slots, resets runtime state, compiles the collision records, spawns the enemy, draws inactive objects and composes the actors; on the first visit to an area below $12 sets its $011B byte and adds a score bonus ($1183 with A=$15); redraws the HUD digits, applies the area's entrance rules ($8C6F), stamps $026D from $E2, sets $0230=$FF and falls into MainTick.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $0230, gameplay zero page, actor/object/projectile arrays, renderer/collision scratch, and display work state.
Hardware: Through its helpers, writes $D021 and the VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen and colour memory.
The Basement's own RenderConditionalSceneVariant ($8CF7): the plain scene, never a variant

Admit one IRQ-produced tick, run the Basement gameplay scheduler in fixed order, and choose the next engine transition
Inputs: IRQ tick $E2 and last stamp $0268; initialized player, enemy, script, event, object, projectile, scene, and transition state
Outputs: stamps $0268; runs timing/input, player, AI, enemy animation, events, scripts, level conditions, objects, boundaries, projectiles, presentation, and resident services; then loops, restarts setup, enters death handling, or begins the level transition
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the union of all scheduled subsystem scratch/state
The Basement's own ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch: the hazard in area 3 and the actor in area 13

Resolve the player's death in The Basement, present the result, and select restart or GAME OVER flow. MainTick comes here when $B4 is set ($86F7); the level exit ($02AF) goes to ResolveLevelCompletion ($87A8), which MainTick jumps to directly
Inputs: death latch $B4, lives $03F2, spare-life flag $03E0 (item 8) and selected object $0279
Outputs: sets $0230=$7F and clears $B4, $B3 and $B6; clears the inactive-object display; LoseLife takes one from the lives; with lives left shows 'N LIVES LEFT' or '1 LIFE REMAINING' (counting the spare life), restores health, reloads the selected spawn and restarts at $8654; with none left spends the spare life if it is held, otherwise renders GAME OVER and restarts the level through ResetSceneAfterDeath ($862E)
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and renderer, delay, object and spawn scratch
Hardware: sets $D021=0 through LoseLife ($8A5E); other display changes occur through called resident/level helpers

ResolveLevelCompletion: runs when the completion request $02AF is set. In this level it asks for no items. Then it adds 5,000 points to the score ($1183 with A = $50: 5 to the thousands digit, 0 to the hundreds), takes away items 13 and 14 (clears $03E5 and $03E6), saves the items, score and clock for the next level (SaveLevelState, $1C30), counts the energy $0229 up from 0 to 21, one step each time the interrupt routine changes $022B, and jumps to the load coordinator at $16AD for the next part.
The Basement adds this call: CopyClockToCode, which copies the clock's minutes and seconds into the last lock's code at $0297

Raise the sprite curtain over the play window and wait until it is gone. Inputs: $0232 is the curtain's lower edge (a raster line, which AnimateStatusPanelReveal at $1F75 lowered) and the interrupt owns the $0231 handshake. Outputs: $0232 is reduced, two lines a frame, below $1D, sprite X expansion is disabled and $0231 is cleared, so the interrupt stops drawing the curtain. Called at the start of the game ($8628), after a lost life ($8762) and after GAME OVER ($879D). Clobbers: A, flags, $0231, and $0232. Hardware: writes VIC-II sprite X-expansion register $D01D.

Reset mutable Basement engine state each time an area is set up: its one caller is $867C, in the area set-up routine that also runs at the start of play and after a lost life. Inputs: the active overlay and resident reset service. Outputs: timers, actor and object flags, arrays, and sentinels are restored to initial values. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad engine state. Hardware: none; the resident call (ResetEngineTickBaselines, $11F1) only copies the tick $E2 into $026C, $026E and $0277, and this body makes no direct I/O write.

Set up the status of a level as it starts. It clears $022B, $022C, $70, $89 and $A0, fills the 30 bytes at $3F92 that keep each area's enemy energy, and both energies ($0229, $022A) with $2C, a full bar, and sets $7A to $69. It copies the item flags saved when the level began ($03B0-$03D7) over the live ones ($03D8-$03FF) and clears $03E9-$03F1 among them, then puts the score ($1CA0) and the clock's digits back from the saved copy ($03CC-$03D7). It sets $87 to $B7, clears $011B-$013E and draws panel picture 0 at both of its places (DrawUiImageRecord, $ABB9, with A = 0 and X = 0, then 1). It builds no scene or wall data. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the drawing routine's scratch.

Take the exit at the edge of the current area; MainTick calls it once a tick, and it does nothing while $0234 is non-zero. Inputs: $0234, current area $A2, player position $54 (across) and $55 (down), and the exit thresholds at $8987. Outputs: when the player is at an edge (Y below 9, Y $BD or more, X $F7 or more, or X below 2) the position becomes a place on the area's edge, counted clockwise from the top left: a quarter of the distance along the edge, plus 0 on the top, $3D on the right, $6A on the bottom and $A7 on the left. The first exit of the area's group in $8987 whose threshold is above that place is installed through InstallSceneStateRecordX ($8939), which moves the player to the destination area and position, or sets the level-exit request $02AF=$FF when the destination is $FF. Away from the edges it returns without change. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install record 0, the level's starting place, as the selected spawn: it loads X with 0 and falls into InstallSceneStateRecordX, whatever the current room. In Basement record 0 is area 1 at X $58, Y $5A, heading 3. Its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8552). Inputs: none. Outputs: $0278=0, and the area, player position, heading, command and redraw latches from record 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install the Basement scene-state/spawn record selected by X.
Inputs: X indexes parallel area, player-coordinate, heading, and command-state arrays at $89AE/$89D5/$89FC/$8A23; callers have already resolved the transition variant and any $0234 gate.
Outputs: A $FF area byte sets $02AF=$FF and returns; otherwise stores X in $0278 and installs area $A2, player coordinates $54/$55/$028E/$028F/$74, heading $68/$69, derived pose $65, command $81, and redraw latches $02A9/$02B8.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $0278, $02AF on the sentinel path, and the installed area/player/redraw state; Y is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Load the selected Basement spawn record into active area, player-position, facing, and transition state
Inputs: $0278 = selected record index; parallel Basement area, X, Y, and packed facing/state tables
Outputs: $A2 = area; $54/$028E = X; $55/$74/$028F = Y; $68/$69 = heading; $65 = $10 or $11 facing-image selector; $81 = packed byte shifted right four; $02A9/$02B8 = $FF; A = $FF; X = selected index
Clobbers: A, X, and processor flags; Y is preserved

39 bytes of exit thresholds. Byte 0 belongs to no area: the scans start at byte 1, and entry 0 of the four tables that follow is the level's start position. Then comes a group for each area, closed by $FF. The routine that finds the exit the player is walking through skips a group for each area before the current one, turns the player's place on the edge of the play window into one number running clockwise round it from the top left, and takes the first value in the group above that number, the closing $FF included. The same index then selects the exit's destination in the four tables that follow.

39 exits, $89AE-$89D4: the area it leads to, or $FF for the way out of the level (entry 37, the first exit of area 14's group), which sets the level-exit request $02AF instead of moving the player. Values: 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 0, 0, 3, 3, 1, 1, 2, 4, 4, 2, 2, 5, 6, 3, 3, 4, 4, 7, 6, 8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9, 13, 11, 10, 12, 11, 14, 10, 255, 13.

39 exits, $8A23-$8A49: the heading in the low three bits, and a command in the high nibble. Values: 3, 1, 1, 1, 1, 5, 5, 3, 3, 5, 5, 7, 3, 3, 7, 7, 1, 5, 7, 7, 5, 1, 5, 1, 3, 3, 7, 5, 7, 1, 3, 5, 1, 3, 7, 1, 7, 255, 5.

The player's death, once the fall is over: it clears $F2, crumbles the sprites away (DissolveSpriteImages, $AC06), lowers the sprite curtain over the play window again (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), waits 25 ticks (WaitEngineTicks, $A14D), clears the play window ($140E), sets the background to black and takes one from the lives, item 26's flag at $03F2. The caller tests the Z flag that the DEC leaves: with no lives left it spends a spare life, item 8, if the player has one, and otherwise the game is over. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.
Impose a short fixed CPU delay. Inputs: none. Outputs: X ends at zero after 128 countdown iterations. Clobbers: X and flags; A and Y are preserved.

Reset The Basement's transient control, actor, object, animation, and AI state to its fixed entry sentinels when the level starts or restarts: its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($8559), not the area set-up. Inputs: No register arguments; the Basement playable occupant and shared zero-page workspace are active. Outputs: Stores $FF to $6C, $02B8, and $84; stores zero to $78, $02AF, $61, $63, $64, $66, $9F, $B3, $B6, $B4, $72, $F2, $7D, $BF, and $0279; stores $71 to $86; A returns $71. Clobbers: A, N, and Z plus the listed RAM state; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Sample and normalize gameplay input and process edge-triggered interface controls for The Basement. Inputs: active-low control-port-2 state, control-port-1/keyboard state, keyboard-select table `$1DA5`, previous edge latches, and current interface state. Outputs: `$7C` bits 0–4 from control-port-2 direction/fire and bit 5 from the POTX threshold, raw keyboard rows `$0260-$0267`, edge latches `$02AA-$02AE/$02BF`, and phase interface/action state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and scanner/interface scratch. Hardware: writes `$FF`, keyboard-row masks, and `$80` to CIA 1 port A `$DC00`; reads `$DC00`, CIA 1 port B `$DC01`, and SID POTX `$D419`; on the F1 edge that switches the music off (`$AA` flipped to zero) it clears SID registers `$D400-$D417`.

Initial sequence byte zero and the current-value indexed base for the hidden-input recognizer at $8C41. Together with the next-byte alias $8C5D it stores 19 values $8C5C-$8C6E; the scanner advances $BF only when normalized input matches the expected change. After the 18th matched change it sets $02AF=$FF, the request to end the level.

Apply the entrance rules for the exit the player arrived by and for the current area. Inputs: $0278, the exit record the player arrived by (an index into the tables at $89AE on), and the current area $A2. Outputs: the entrance animation's kind and length from the list at $8CC3 go to $0293/$0294 (kind 0 when $0278 is not listed); exit $17 sets $74=$98 and $EF=$FF; in area $0D with item flag $03E9 set, the first collision coordinate is copied ($F7EA to $F7EC) and it returns; otherwise InitializeRoomSpecificEntranceState installs the AI scripts and sprite colours of areas $0A, $0E, $0F, $10 and $11. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI-script state. Hardware: writes the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 directly in areas $0A, $0E, $10 and $11.

The Basement's own entrance rules, chosen by the area number in Y: area 3 sets the two sprite multicolours $D025 and $D026 to 11 and 12 (dark and middle grey) and $F8 to 9, for the moving hazard there; area 13 starts animation $C626 in the second actor's slot, or $C62D once flag $03EA is set (item 18), and sets $F8 to $0B. Any other area returns. ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch at $97C6 acts on $F8 every pass of the main loop.

The Basement's entrance-animation list, three bytes an entry as in Central Park's (the exit the player arrived by, the kind of entrance, how many animation steps it lasts), ending with $FF. This level's has no entries: only the $FF.

Mark all eight actor slots inactive and clear their key state bytes. Inputs: none. Outputs: $61, $63, and the corresponding $0210 and $0248 slot arrays are cleared. Clobbers: A is zero, Y exits as $FF, and flags change; X is preserved.

The address ApplySceneEntryRules reads the third byte of an entrance-animation entry from ($8C85, with X stepping by three). With the list at $8CC3 empty the read never happens here; the address is the operand of ClearActorSlots's first instruction.

Copy the 1000-byte screen-color staging image into C64 color RAM. Inputs: staging bytes $0800-$0BE7 and visible C64 I/O. Outputs: color RAM $D800-$DBE7 receives the corresponding low nybbles; the last 24 cells of the third page are harmlessly copied twice. Clobbers: A, X, and flags; X returns zero. Hardware: writes color RAM $D800-$DBE7.

Provide The Basement's reserved per-tick runtime hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing gameplay state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Provide The Basement's reserved presentation-initialization hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing presentation state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

RTS: where The Basement's title load points PlayNextLoadVector at $3FF6. The one call through that vector, from StartLevelLoad (engine $1405), comes once as the game starts, before any level is loaded, and goes through the engine's own JMP $0E00 there, so this RTS is never reached.
RenderConditionalSceneVariant: The Basement draws the plain scene of the current area ($A2) every time, with none of the variants Central Park chooses with its flags.

When the player's level-condition latch is active and no player animation script is running, force zero health and install the facing-specific terminal animation
Inputs: condition latch $B6, player animation-pointer high byte $61, and facing byte $69; animation streams begin at $BBA0 and $BB94
Outputs: sets player health $0229=0 and tail-installs one of the two terminal animation streams; otherwise returns unchanged
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the state changed by InstallAnimation

Hide the parts of an actor's sprites that are behind the current area's foreground pictures, then stage the sprites. Inputs: X is the first sprite slot to process (0 for the player, 4 for the other actor, or an auxiliary slot); it works up to slot 3, or slot 7 when X is 4 or more. A is the actor's depth ($74 or $74,X), compared with byte 1 of each 4-byte record in the area's list (pointers at $8FD1, an $FF ends a list; a record is a picture's scene index, a depth, a column and a row). Outputs: for each drawn slot ($0218 bit 4 or 6 set, $0210 non-zero), every record whose depth is at least A is tested by TestSceneConditionRecord ($8DD4): where the picture overlaps the 24-by-21 sprite, the sprite's pixel pairs under the picture's non-zero pixels are cleared and $0218 bit 4 is set. Then, with interrupts off, each slot with $0218 bit 6 gets its position, pointer ($30 or $38 plus the slot) and colour bits staged in $0240, $0258 and $0250, and $0210 is copied to $0248. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and masking scratch.

Mask one foreground picture out of a sprite slot. Inputs: ($ED) points at the area's list of 4-byte records (scene index, depth, column, row) and Y at the depth byte of one of them; $1F is the sprite slot, and $F4/$F6 and $F5 its X (low and high bytes) and Y. Outputs: the record's picture is placed at column x 8 and row x 8 + $1A, with the width and height from its header byte; if it does not overlap the 24-by-21 sprite the routine returns at once, otherwise it sets bit 4 of the slot's $0218 and clears, in the slot's sprite image, every pixel pair that lies under a non-zero pixel pair of the picture. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $04-$07, $1C/$1D, $21/$22, $25/$26, $8C/$8D, $D7-$DB and the slot's sprite image.

24 entries: eight zeroes, eight ones and eight twos. $8F02/$8F18/$8F2E/$8F44 use clipped horizontal pixel X to select the destination byte within a three-byte sprite row. Paired with the clearing masks at $8FB8; X advances two hires pixels per multicolor source pair.

24 entries: $3F,$3F,$CF,$CF,$F3,$F3,$FC,$FC repeated for three sprite bytes. The scene-condition renderer ANDs these into the selected sprite-row byte whenever the corresponding source pixel pair is nonzero. This removes a two-bit pair, selected jointly with the byte-offset lookup at $8FA0. Ends at $8FCF; $8FD0 is a zero byte between it and the pointer directory, which no instruction reads.

ServiceEnemyBoundaryLatch, The Basement's version, called from MainTick every pass: it does nothing while $F8 is zero, and otherwise runs the hazard or actor that the entrance rules at $8C95 chose for the area. $F8 = 9 is the moving hazard in area 3 (below) and $0B the actor in area 13 ($9850).

Area 3 ($F8 = 9). This code moves the second actor itself, with no animation ($63 is kept at zero): once two or more counts of the interrupt counter $E2 have passed since the time kept in $0277, it moves the actor 4 left and 1 down for each count, then draws it (ComposeEnemySprites with X = 4) and tests the scene conditions for it at its Y, so the scenery can hide it.

Puts the actor back at the start, X $AC and Y $5A, keeps the time in $0277 and clears its animation $63. It comes here when the actor's X is below 8, and when a step of 4 to the left would take X below zero.
two counts or more since the last step?

Unless the player's action, $6D with its two low bits cleared, is $0C, the player dies ($B6 = $FF) when they are inside the hazard's reach: their X plus $30 less the actor's X must be below $50 (from 48 left of it to 31 right of it), and that distance divided by four picks a pair of limits from the tables at $98AB and $98BF that the player's Y plus 12 less the actor's Y must fall between.
within reach across?

Area 13 ($F8 = $0B). Nothing happens once flag $03EA (item 18) is set, or while the second actor has an animation. Otherwise the actor answers to where the player stands, with its state in $03EC (the byte Central Park uses for item 20's flag). In state 0, a player at Y $75 or more and X $93 or more makes it play $C634 (frames 101 to 103) and go to state 1. In state 1, a player who steps back below X $93 makes it play $C63D (frames 102, 101 and 100) and go back to state 0, and one at X $A8 or more makes it play $C646 and go to state 2: frames 106 to 113, moving it 29 to the left, with event 13 (EventDamagePlayer2c, $2C energy off the player) on its second step. In state 2, a player below X $93 makes it play $C63D and go back to state 0. MovePlayer at $9F72 keeps the player from passing it while it is in state 2.

The lower limits of the hazard's reach in area 3, twenty bytes, one for each four pixels across: the player's Y plus 12 less the hazard's Y must be at least this. The $FF at either end leaves no room, so those columns are safe; between them the limits fall from 13 to 5 and rise again, and with the upper limits at $98BF they make a diamond.

The upper limits of the hazard's reach, twenty bytes read with the same index: the player's Y plus 12 less the hazard's Y must be below this. They rise from 14 to 20 and fall back to 13, with 0 at either end.

Run The Basement's fixed animation at $BC6B the requested number of times, run the finishing animation at $BC80 once, then synchronize three engine-tick stamps. Inputs: A is a nonzero repetition count; animation streams $BC6B and $BC80, actor state, the blocking runtime loop, and resident tick-snapshot helper $11F1 are active. Outputs: Each $BC6B cycle is installed and serviced until $61 clears; $BC80 is then installed and serviced once; finally $026C, $026E, and $0277 receive the current engine tick $E2 and A returns that tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, transient stack contents, animation/runtime state, and $026C/$026E/$0277. Hardware: Through the blocking runtime loop, advances sprite/display state and reads controls; this wrapper and the $11F1 timer-snapshot tail perform no direct I/O.

Install an animation and run the blocking script runtime loop. Inputs: A:X is the animation pointer and the actor context is valid. Outputs: the animation is installed and the runtime loop completes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and runtime state. Hardware: changes sprite presentation indirectly through the engine.

Run script-time engine frames until the active actor or action completes. Inputs: an installed animation and valid runtime state. Outputs: enemy AI, auxiliary sprites, input, and animation state advance until $61 clears. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad frame scratch. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly and reads input through the called joystick poller.

Advance the player's and then the enemy's animation by one eligible engine step, at most once a tick. Inputs: tick $E2 and timer slot 2 ($026A, interval 1 at $9D20); both actors' animation state. Outputs: when no tick has passed since the last call the gate at $9D0A returns straight to RunScriptRuntimeLoop; otherwise AnimationInterpreter ($A05E, X=0) steps the player's animation, and ScheduleEnemyAnimation ($A049) steps the enemy's when its own tick has advanced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation scratch.

Execute a scripted action for a fixed number of completed animation cycles. Inputs: A is the repetition count and actor facing and animation state are valid. Outputs: the count is exhausted and scripted state advances. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, and $0234. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly.

Between steps it runs ScheduleEnemyAnimation and RuntimeNoOpHook. Script command 31. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here and then runs its scripted coordinate sequence, The Basement calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $9C42 instead. That returns with A zero, so this always goes on to $9C38, which sets X to $07 and Y to 2 (values only the missing sequence would have read) and goes on into the same routine again: the player loses two points of energy twice and the command is cleared. No wall in The Basement carries command 31, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.
