$FF in place of an area: the end of the 16 object records that start at $B88C.

ObjectNeedsItem14OrDie: the routine object records 11 and 12 (area 12) call. With item 14 selected it sets flag $03EB to $FF and returns with Y = 14 and Z set, so ObjectEngine goes on with item 14 in place of the record's item 19: that item is held already, so its flag stays as it is, and the record's scene $B9D4 is drawn, 500 points are added to the score ($1183 with A = 5, the hundreds digit) and picture 14 is drawn again in the panel's second box, green now (DrawUiImageRecord, $ABDC). With any other item selected it sets $B6 to $FF, so the player dies, and returns Y = $FF, which ObjectEngine takes as nothing to take.

ObjectUseItem13OpenWall: the routine object record 15 (area 14) calls. With item 13 selected it copies the first wall's start X ($F7EA) into its end X ($F7EC), so that the first wall of area 14, the short one at 196, 119, ends where it begins and no longer stops the player, and returns with A zero, which lets the take of item 17 go ahead. Otherwise it returns with Z clear and nothing happens.

ObjectNeedsGreenItem14: the routine object records 13 and 14 (area 13) call. Only with item 14 selected and flag $03EB set (item 14 turned green in area 12) does it start animation $C664 in the second actor's slot (the lunge of $C646 without its event, then frames 104, 105, 102, 101 and 100) and return with A zero, which lets the take of item 18 go ahead; once item 18 is held the actor in area 13 no longer answers to the player. Otherwise it returns $FF, and nothing is taken.

CopyClockToCode, which The Basement's ResolveLevelCompletion calls after SaveLevelState ($1C30): for X from 3 down to 0 it takes the offset at $1D41,X (10, 11, 20 and 21, entries 2 to 5 of clock_digit_offsets) and copies the clock digit at $1C77 plus that offset, the two digits of the minutes and the two of the seconds, into $0297,X. The Office shows the four as a code in area 3 (ObjectShowCode, $B8EF there) and The Final Battle's lock opens only to them (ObjectEnterCode, $B327 there): the clock's minutes and seconds at the end of this level are the code for the last one, unless a GAME OVER in The Office replaces them with the clock at that moment (its own CopyClockToCode, $B922 there).

Draw the picture of the first object record of the current area ($A2) whose item is still in place. It scans the 14-byte records from $B88C to the $FF that ends them, passing over those of other areas, those whose item's flag ($03D8 plus the record's byte 11) is set, and those with no picture (bytes 5 and 6 of the record, a high byte of 0), and tail-enters the scene renderer ($81E4) with the first one left in $02/$03: at most one picture is drawn. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $02/$03, and the renderer's scratch when it draws.

Expire a displayed inactive object after 100 engine ticks. Inputs: creation or display tick $A0 and current tick $E2. Outputs: the object remains or is cleared and its UI is refreshed. Clobbers: A, flags, and the clear helper's clobbers on expiry. Hardware: changes UI or display memory on expiry.

Remove the inactive-object display and redraw its status image. Inputs: current inactive-object and UI state. Outputs: $A0 is cleared and the corresponding UI image is rendered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and renderer scratch. Hardware: changes hardware-visible UI bitmap, screen, and color RAM.

The RTS that ends the Basement playable phase's inactive-object expiry check. The branches at $BA21 and $BA25 come here when the delay has not elapsed or no inactive object is pending, and ClearInactiveObjectAndRefreshUi also ends here after redrawing the panel's image.
Inputs: A valid return address is on the stack.
Outputs: Returns; on the two branch paths nothing has been cleared or redrawn.
Clobbers: Registers, flags, object state, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.

Periodically render the alternating active-state image for the first eligible object in the current area
Inputs: timer slot 5; phase counter $A9; current area $A2; 14-byte records at $B88C; persistent active bytes $03D8,Y; two active scene pointers in record bytes 5-6 and 7-8
Outputs: on an admitted tick decrements $A9, selects one of the two active pointers by $A9 bit 0, loads it into $02/$03, and tail-enters the recursive renderer; clears $A9 and returns when no eligible object remains
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $A9, $02/$03, and scene-renderer scratch on a render path

Eight pointers, one for each kind of extra sprite the enemy can carry: none, $E1B1, $E1B1, $E1B1, $E1B1, $E9D9, $F180, $F180. The extra sprite is part of the enemy's figure, not its weapon (the weapon is the frame's alternative slot, picked by the low two bits of $92): for the frames the pose table covers the composer draws it in the enemy's first sprite, in place of the frame's first slot and at the position of its second, and sets the attributes of the enemy's first three sprites from $E170. The high nibble of the area's entry in the enemy table at $AE3B picks the pointer: it is twice the kind, a byte offset into this table. The composer adds a word offset taken from the pose table to the chosen pointer, reads the word there and unpacks the image it leads to, the same way for every kind. No area's enemy has a kind whose pointer is $F180, the unpacked images.
